description: Five-dimension bank-quality score per bank-year. Each metric is percentile-ranked against SAME-YEAR peers in this dataset, so a score is relative to the sector in that year, not to an absolute standard. Dimension score is the mean of its metric percentiles; composite is the mean of available dimensions, and is null unless at least three dimensions could be scored.
methodology_warning: This framework deliberately does NOT score reported profit directly, and profitability is only one of five dimensions. The reason is specific to this dataset: in FY2024-FY2025 several banks reported a profit while leaving most of their non-performing book unprovided, so any earnings-weighted ranking inverts the true ordering - it rewards under-provisioning. The solvency_risk dimension (unprovided NPLs against equity) is what separates a bank that recognised its losses from one that deferred them. hard_fail_flags override the composite entirely and produce grade FAIL: these are not merely poor scores but states of not meeting the regulatory capital floor, and a bank can hold a respectable composite while failing. Scores are also only as comparable as the underlying basis - see reporting_basis on each row and the comparability warning in _cross_bank.json.

hard_fail_definitions.below_10pct_capital_minimum: Reported CRAR below the 10% Basel III minimum.
hard_fail_definitions.unprovided_npls_exceed_equity: Classified loans minus provision held exceeds shareholders equity, i.e. fully providing would erase the capital base.
hard_fail_definitions.npl_above_20pct: More than a fifth of the loan book classified.
hard_fail_definitions.loss_making: Reported a loss after tax for the year.
